## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In Abhidharma studies, scholars such as Ryūjō Yamada have cited the tenfold groupings found in the *Okkanta Saṁyutta* as potential early scriptural precursors to systematic Abhidharma classifications of mental factors (*mahābhūmika*) [Gyatso 1992; Willemen et al. 1998].
Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal links across the Pali canon, recording 890 matches across 52 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest correspondences occur with the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), *Sotāpatti Saṁyutta* (SN 55), *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), *Diṭṭhi Saṁyutta* (SN 24), *Uppāda Saṁyutta* (SN 26), and *Rāhula Saṁyutta* (SN 18) [DharmaNexus]. Across canonical languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of SN 25 with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicles 3 and 6) and *Madhyamāgama* (T 26), Sanskrit compendia including the *Dharmasaṁgraha* and *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, and Tibetan translations of the *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* [DharmaNexus].
